```
/// A suite made on the program layer: the program whose entry runs each case under the runner and
/// says the tally, and each case as the entry calls it.
export type MadeSuite = { lowered: Lowered, cases: List<CaseCall> }

/// The suite of every case `files` write, made: each case's body reached and lowered as a unit, the
/// bodies they reach made with them, and the entry the suite's runner builds — the one every build
/// of a suite shares — over the cases in the files' order. Absent where it isn't made yet, said why.
export fn made_suite(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    files: List<SourceFileAddress>,
    placed: fn(SourceFileAddress) -> string,
) -> Result<MadeSuite, string> {
    let found = flatten(
        [[CaseFound { file: f, at: c, k: k } for k, c in file_cases(engine, f).cases] for f in files],
    )
    let calls = [found_called(c) for c in found]
    let root = suite_root(calls)
    let survey = task_survey(engine)
    let made = made_reaching(
        survey,
        root,
        ENTRY,
        [],
        scheduled_by(survey, root),
        null,
        null,
        [],
        files.first()?.package_name,
    )
    let lowered = match made {
        .Made(l) -> l,
        .Unmade(why, at) -> { fail "${why}, at ${at}" },
        .Refused(fs) -> { fail "a body it reaches holds a node its seat refused, in ${[spelled_file(f) for f in fs].join(", ")}" },
    }
    let cases = [CaseCall { symbol: c.called.symbol, label: c.label } for c in [CaseLabelled { called: calls[i], label: case_label(found[i], placed) } for i in 0..found.length]]
    let main = suite_entry(lowered.types, cases, [])
    .Ok(
        MadeSuite {
            lowered: lowered with { entry: main.body with { layouts: [layout_of_entry(main.types, t) for t in main.body.reg_types], seats: [], answer: Layout.Word }, externs: lowered.externs.concat(runner_rows) },
            cases: cases,
        },
    )
}

/// A case a file writes, beside the file and its place among the file's cases.
type CaseFound = { file: SourceFileAddress, at: CaseAt, k: int }
```

```
/// should call, but it never traps the compiler on a shape it was
/// never built for) — `problems` is what actually stops the build,
/// spoken as real diagnostics at the declaration itself.
/// `@unique(a, b, …)` on a `@model` type: no two rows hold the same values in those fields together —
/// a key over several columns, declared on the model itself. Its fields are the type's own, named
/// bare and checked where they're written; each must be a column the model stores, and named once.
/// A key declared twice is `@model`'s to refuse, once.
export fn unique(t: Type, ..fields: List<Field>) -> List<Diagnostic> {
    let key = [f.name for f in fields]
    let at = key_written(t, key)?.at
    if key.is_empty() { return [model_key_empty(t, at)] }
    [model_key_unstored(t, n, at) for n in key if !stored(t).any(it.name == n)]
        .concat([model_key_repeats(t, n, at) for j, n in key if key.index_of(n) < j])
}

/// The `@unique` the type `t` wears over the fields `key`, in their order.
fn key_written(t: Type, key: List<string>) -> Annotation? { t.annotations.find(it.name == "unique" && it.args.join(",") == key.join(",")) }

/// The keys a `@model` type declares on itself, `@unique(a, b, …)`, each as the fields it names.
fn model_keys(t: Type) -> List<List<string>> { [a.args for a in t.annotations if a.name == "unique" && !a.args.is_empty()] }

export fn model(t: Type) -> Declared {
    Declared { made: Model.derive(t), problems: shape_problems(t) }
}
```

```
/// `@unique(a, b, …)` on a `@model` type: no two rows hold the same values in those fields together —
/// a key over several columns, declared on the model itself. Its fields are the type's own, named
/// bare and checked where they're written; each must be a column the model stores, and named once.
/// A key of one field is that field's own `@unique` mark, refused here. A key declared twice is `@model`'s to refuse, once.
export fn unique(t: Type, ..fields: List<Field>) -> List<Diagnostic> {
    let key = [f.name for f in fields]
    let at = key_written(t, key)?.at
    if key.is_empty() { return [model_key_empty(t, at)] }
    let problems = [model_key_unstored(t, n, at) for n in key if !stored(t).any(it.name == n)]
        .concat([model_key_repeats(t, n, at) for j, n in key if key.index_of(n) < j])
    if problems.is_empty() && key.length == 1 { return [model_key_single(t, key[0], at)] }
    problems
}
```

```
/// crosses back into compiler-owned data. The one scan `world_reached`
/// renders as prose and `world_witness` reads the chain off of.
type WorldHit = { row: Ins, body: Body }

fn world_hit(l: Lowered, permits_embed: bool) -> WorldHit? {
    let rows = rt_index()
    for b in l.fns.concat([l.entry]) {
        let hit = world_in(rows, b, permits_embed)
        if hit != null { return WorldHit { row: hit!, body: b } }
    }
    null
}

/// What a compile-time run reaches of the world, worded: the row, the body it stands in as
/// `spelled` names a body to its reader — none where it is the run's own entry, which the verdict's
/// label already names — and each call link back to the entry. Null when nothing reaches it.
export fn world_reached(
    l: Lowered,
    permits_embed: bool,
    spelled: fn(string) -> string = as_symbolled,
) -> string? {
    let hit? = world_hit(l, permits_embed) else { return null }
    let row = hosted_symbol(hit.row) ?? ""
    let reach: Reach = rt_index().get(row)?.reach ?? Reach.World
    let stands_in = if hit.body.name == l.entry.name { "" } else { " in `${spelled(hit.body.name)}`" }
    let said = if reach is .Embed { "embeds a file${stands_in}, but this compile-time call cannot return build inputs" } else { "reaches `${row}`${stands_in}" }
    // The refusal names each CALL LINK, not only the body the
    // world row stands in: `f` called from `g` called from the
    // const's entry reads as the chain the reader wrote.
    "${said}${callers_from(l, hit.body.name, spelled)}"
}
```

```
/// Where a symbol's file ends and its name begins.
const SOURCE_SPELLED: string = ".av."

/// Where a symbol's package ends and its file's path in the package's sources begins.
const SOURCE_DIR: string = "/src/"

/// A const a body declares at `s` of `store`, its value of type `ty` reading, of what the body binds,

/// the binary's own data.
fn body_const_value(
    engine: QueryEngine,
    file: SourceFileAddress,
    store: SyntaxArena,
    unit: string,
    s: StmtId,
    ty: SignedType,
    seeds: List<ConstSeed>,
    frame: int? = null,
) -> NamedValue {
    let settled = body_const_settlement(engine, file, store, unit, s, ty, seeds, frame)
    let why = settled.unsettled
    if why != null { return NamedValue.Unsettled(why!) }
    NamedValue.Settled(settled.words, settled.data!)
}
```

```
export fn unknown_variant(owner: string, variant: string, variants: List<string>, asked: bool) -> Voice {
    Voice {
        message: "`${owner}` has no variant `${variant}`",
        label: if asked { "asked here" } else { "matched here" },
        help: variant_meant(variant, variants),
    }

/// A `match` testing variants of a value of `found`, which is no enum.
export fn unenumerated_match(found: string) -> Voice {

        label: "built here",
        help: "annotate the binding, return it from a fn that declares the type, or write `Type.${name}`",
    }
}
```

```
/// A program refused EXACTLY ONCE, saying `phrase`. The count is not
/// optional here — one mistake earns one message, so a refusal test

export fn refused_with(source: string, phrase: string) -> bool {
    let a = judged(source)

}

/// A program that refuses to RUN, saying `phrase`: the evaluator's refusal of a program its build
/// accepts, or the one thing its build says of what it runs before any program does — a const's
/// settling — and never a cascade.
export fn refused_at_run(source: string, phrase: string) -> bool {
    let a = judged(source)
    if a.diagnostics.length > 1 { return false }
    match a.run() { .Err(msg) -> msg.contains(phrase), .Ok(_) -> false }
}
```

```
# A derived record's edit, over a package of its own: three records each deriving one trait in one
# file, the middle one given a field. Only its site runs its generator again.
derived_edit() {
    pkg="$tmp/derived"
    mkdir -p "$pkg/src"
    printf '[package]\nname = "derived"\nversion = "0.0.1"\n' >"$pkg/avra.toml"
    printf 'use @std.meta.{Type, Directive}\n\nexport trait Count {\n    static fn derive(t: Type) -> List<Directive> {\n        [Directive { twin: "", name: t.name, at: t.at, source: quote { impl ${t} { static fn count() -> int { ${t.fields.length} } } } }]\n    }\n}\n' >"$pkg/src/count.av"
    body() { printf 'use @std.meta.{derive}\nuse count.{Count}\n\n@derive(Count)\ntype A = { a: int }\n\n@derive(Count)\ntype B = { %s }\n\n@derive(Count)\ntype C = { c: int }\n\nprintln("${A.count()} ${B.count()} ${C.count()}")\n' "$1" >"$pkg/src/main.av"; }
    made() { "$avra" build "$pkg" >"$tmp/log" 2>&1 || { echo "witness_program_edit: the derived build failed:" >&2; tail -5 "$tmp/log" >&2; exit 1; }; unsigned_at "$pkg/src/main" "$1" ""; }
    afresh() { find "$pkg/.avra-cache" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || :; find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete; }
    body 'b: int'
    afresh
    made "$tmp/derived.base"
    body 'b: int, b2: int'
    AVRA_QUERY_TIMES=1 AVRA_FOLD_CHECK=1 made "$tmp/derived.warm"
    asked=$(grep -oE '(^|[ ,;])generated [0-9.]+s / [0-9.]+s \([0-9]+\)' "$tmp/log" | grep -oE '\([0-9]+\)' | tr -d '()')
    afresh
    made "$tmp/derived.cold"
```

```
//! A component a derive emits and `View` refuses is refused where the derive's
//! template wrote it. The member's place crosses to the second derive with the
//! file its offset indexes, so the refusal speaks at the template and the
//! compiler is never wrecked by reading it against the file the code landed in.
//! `avra_ran` and `scratch_dir` are the neighbouring tests' own.
use @std.io.{make_dirs, write_text}
use @std.time.{stamp}

/// A derive that emits a composition marking its member `@attr`.
```

```
# Net-off rehearsal: AVRA_PROGRAM_NET defaults to 0 (report only, not landed)

The rehearsal is branch `net-off-rehearsal` = a049f416 + 50421e61. The commit changes two things:
- `packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av`: `program_net()` is now `env("AVRA_PROGRAM_NET") == "1"`, where it was `!= "0"`. Every command (`build`, `run`, `check`, `test`, `tapes`, `db`) reaches the net only through `net_said` → `program_net()`, so this is the CLI's one switch.
- `tools/gate.sh` `slice_cli`: the forced `export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1` around the cli suite is gone, so the suite runs on the new default. The gate already exported NET=0 for every other row.

Rows that explicitly measure the net were left as they are, because they are claims about the net itself:
- the build slice's net-on cli builds
- the findings slices' NET=1 false-refusal count

Every gate slice was run on gen-2 of 50421e61: 37 slices, which cover the cli suite and the std suites (program, doors-a/b, findings-a..d).
- The run was stopped once at the 2-hour background cap during refusal-c, and was resumed in two chunks.
- Tree: 4 cores, `AVRA_MAX_COMPILES=16`, `AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=14000`.

| fmt | fmt-changed: `net_off_a_doubled…/src/main.av` lex.error | the deliberately malformed fixture. Fixed by e1a3b930 (batch 57), which this branch doesn't carry | no |
| cost | `snapshot 161e52bf… is not in this clone and could not be fetched` | the environment (a shallow clone) | no |
| cli | 9 unpinned cases from 5 test files, below | the net | **yes, all 9** |

Every other slice is PASS: avrac-a..g, program, idioms ×3, sound, doors-a/b, findings-a..d (0 refusals), refusal-a..c, witness-b, warnings-a..c, edit-a..g and build.

### The cli suite's 9: 6 cases where the net hid a real layer gap, 1 a stream difference, 2 a doubled refusal

Each case was rebuilt by hand from its test's own fixture and run with NET=0 against NET=1. **(F)** means a real layer gap that the net was masking.

1. **`sibling_programs_test` :62, :65 (2 cases): F, layer-commands.** A package whose module file `src/stray/stray.av` runs a statement (`println("stray")`) is BUILT and RUN by the layer: exit 0, prints `alpha`. The old path refuses it with `lower.entry_only` ("only the entry … runs statements"). **The layer is missing the entry-only law for a module file reached by `run`/`build` of a lone entry.**
2. **`generated_view_test` :29, :33 (2 cases): F, annotations (mine).** A derive that emits a composition marking its member `@attr` is ACCEPTED by the layer (exit 0). The old path refuses it with `@std/ui:marked-composition` at the template (`formed.av:12:47`). **The second derive (`View`) is never run over a component a first derive emitted.** The old path also says a spurious `type.impl` "`impl ${0}` serves no declared type" in std-ui's view.av, which is its own defect.
3. **`ui_view_test` :167, :173 (undelivered, 2 cases): F, values/consts (mine).** A user slider declaring `press`, drawn on a page, is ACCEPTED by the layer (exit 0). The old path refuses it with `const.trap` on std-ui's `const web_seats` (realize/html/delivery.av:32), whose trap words are the law ("a page names nothing that delivers a `slider`'s `press`…"). **The layer doesn't settle a library const over the user program's rows, or doesn't refuse its trap.**
4. **`build_report_test` :38 (1 case): F, layer-commands, small.** The layer's `build` and `run` print their refusals on **stderr**, while `check`, the old path and the net print on stdout. The test reads stdout, so it sees no headers. Both refusals are said, with the right kinds and places.
   - Same on a package: build/run net=0 → stdout 0 / stderr 1, and net=1 → stdout 1 / stderr 0. `check` → stdout either way.
   - Fix: refusals go to one stream for every command, as `check` does.
   - Side note: under `avra test` this case is red with NET=1 too. There the net's old-path judge runs on the suite's virtual clock and gives up, so the layer answers alone. Worth a look when the net goes, though it goes with the net.
5. **`ui_view_test` :75, :76 (refused parts, 2 cases): R, recommend L.** The layer says all 24 of the library's refusals in the same order, plus one more: `type.variant_lit: Prim has no variant Nope` at `@prim(.Nope)`, beside `@std/ui:not-a-prim` at the same mark. If the lead wants one refusal per mark, it's F (mine): an annotation argument's type refusal stands down when the reading law refuses the same argument.
```

```
built clean and trapped only at run time; the old path settles it at compile time and refuses.

gathers it (`value_run` takes the program into `made_reaching`). `gathered_broken_found` finds,
at the const's value, the settlement law its run broke, handed what `settles_broken` hands. The
voice is the const law's own (const_trapped, const_over_budget, const_reaching).
`program_gathered` keeps those findings per file and program. `program_erring` and
`entry_erring` count them, and `file_law_diags` says them for a ProgramFile that names its
program (tapes' `program_file` and the held suite's `named`). The Found→LawFinding constructor
is now the one `finding_of` both paths share.
```

```
    /// `boxes` among the `dyn` boxes the program makes; a round that meets one it hadn't is
    /// unsettled, since a `dyn` call walked before may hold one of them.
    fn met(boxes: List<BoxMark>) {
        let known = self.boxes.get()
        let new = [b for b in boxes if !known.any((k) -> same_box(k, b))]
        if new.is_empty() { return }
        self.boxes.set(known.concat(new))
        self.unsettled.set(true)
    }

    /// `c` among the declared fns the program takes as values; a round that meets one it hadn't is
    /// unsettled, since a call through a fn value walked before may be it.
    fn valued(c: CalledFn) {
        if self.values.get().any(it.symbol == c.symbol) { return }
        self.values.push(c)
        self.unsettled.set(true)
    }
```

```
fn narrowed(engine: QueryEngine, file: SourceFileAddress, at: int, cx: Copies, left: ExprId) -> bool {
    let step? = cx.store.place_step(left) else { return false }

fn let_never_absent(cx: Copies, name: string, at: ExprId) -> bool {
```

```
//! THE UNBOUNDED CLEANUP LAW: a `defer` or `errdefer` runs under the
//! shield a cold exit raises, so a wait in its body is bounded by the
//! `within` that body writes and by nothing else. A body that PARKS —
//! reaches a cancel point, the settled cancel fact (`cancel_reach.av`)
//! — outside every `within` it writes is refused: the wait would
//! outlast the thing it was cleaning and no bound would cut it.
//!
//! Run at lowering, where the cancel fact is settled
//! (`Program.lowered_bodies` touches it first): judging earlier would
//! read a half-built answer.

/// One wait in a deferred body that parks outside every `within` the
/// body writes, and the node it stands at.
type Unbounded = { node: ExprId, wait: NodeWait }

impl Workspace {
    /// Every unbounded cleanup in the program's files, one refusal per
    /// deferred statement.
    fn cleanup_voices(files: List<FileId>) -> List<Diag> {
        flatten(
            [self.cleanup_of(d) for f in files for d in self.decls.decls_of_file(f) if self.cancel_member(d)],
        )
    }

    /// One declaration's deferred statements, judged.
    fn cleanup_of(d: DeclId) -> List<Diag> {
        let s = self.cancel_survey(d)
        let store = s.view.store
        let tag = store.tag_stmt(Stmt.Defer(ExprId { index: 0 }, false))
```

```
//! The laws a type test keeps: its subject is a `dyn` (read through a
//! name, as any read is), the type it names is ONE concrete type — a
//! box's tag names a type with its arguments, so it tells no `dyn`,
//! absence, type parameter or built-in generic apart, but it does tell one
//! instance of a declared generic from another — and that type implements the
//! `dyn`'s trait. The binder answers the named type, recorded on the
//! pattern's read for lowering to test against.
use core.{PatId, Type, TypeId, TypeRef, DeclId}
use features.{TypeCx, this_is}
use diagnostics.{Voice, defect_at, refusal, said_as}

export fn narrow_types(mut cx: TypeCx, p: PatId, ty: TypeRef, expected: TypeId) -> List<TypeId> {
    let tr? = cx.view.types.dyn_trait(cx.seen(expected)) else { return not_dyn(cx, p, expected) }
    let to = cx.written_in_pattern(cx.view.origin_of_pat(p), cx.pat_loc(p), ty)
    if cx.view.types.shape_of(to) is .Error { return [to] }
    let fault? = untaggable(cx.view.types.shape_of(to)) else { return implementing(cx, p, to, tr, expected) }
    refused_target(cx, p, fault, to, tr)
}

/// The named type, once the tag can tell it: it implements the trait.
fn implementing(mut cx: TypeCx, p: PatId, to: TypeId, tr: DeclId, expected: TypeId) -> List<TypeId> {
    if !cx.implements_decl(to, tr) { return not_implementor(cx, p, to, tr, expected) }
    let read? = cx.view.store.name_read(p) else { return unread(cx, p, to) }
    cx.facts.set_type(read, to)
    [to]
}
```

```
fn default_law(

    cx.emit(total_arm_last(cx, after))
    true
}

}
```
